thread:
gina_sales: EmeraldMed POC ask: Private deployment. Compliance demands preserved L3 source IPs for IDS, mTLS to connector preferred, and minimal CIDR exposure. Also asking how static egress IPs affect pricing. Quick guidance?

omar_se: TL;DR: mTLS supported. L3 preservation needs peering/TGW/direct routing. PrivateLink is fastest but connector will SNAT so L3 changes to connector ENI. If they cannot accept X-Forwarded-For, plan peering.

lina_netops: Quick options:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint): minimal firewall work, DNS/private ENI; source IP becomes connector ENI (NAT). Fast for POC.
- VPC peering or TGW: preserves source IPs. Requires route table updates, SG changes, symmetric routing. More ops but meets IDS requirement.

ben_platform: Pricing notes: managed static egress IPs = one-time setup + monthly per-EIP + small per-GB surcharge. Dedicated reserved capacity can include IPs at a discount. Peering itself doesn't change Redwood fees but cloud TGW/transfer costs may apply.

lina_netops: Minimal firewall allowlist for initial PrivateLink POC (confirm EIPs with infra):
```
- Outbound TCP 443 to: 52.37.18.101, 52.37.18.102 (Redwood test ENIs)
- DNS UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver
- NTP UDP 123
- Allow ephemeral return ports 1024-65535 if NATted
- Allow ICMP type 3/4 for PMTU discovery
```
Recommend FQDN privatelink entries if their NGFW supports it, but IPs are stronger.

omar_se: Fast POC plan: 1) Stand up PrivateLink + short-lived mTLS certs for functional tests. 2) Parallel design for peering/TGW to preserve L3 if required. POC can validate app behavior while peering is implemented.

gina_sales: EmeraldMed insists on L3 preservation for audit. Can we turn around peering design quickly?

lina_netops: Yes but needs their netops to agree CIDRs and provide firewall contact. Design review 1-2 business days, infra ticket to provision routes. Aim to complete before their test window.

omar_se: Curl snippets for their team (replace certs):
```bash
# mTLS health check
curl --cert poc-client.crt --key poc-client.key -v https://emerald.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/healthz
# non-mTLS
curl -v https://emerald.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/healthz
```
If moving to peering, disable SNAT toward connector subnets to preserve src IPs.

ben_platform: Action items for sales: 1) Lina to share test EIPs + allowlist by EOD, 2) Omar to prepare short-lived certs and test script, 3) Ben to email rough pricing delta for managed egress vs reserved bundle. I'll flag infra freeze windows if provisioning timeline hits them.
